pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Arkansas Department of Labor and Licensing oversees the licensing process for electricians, and the Board contracts with Prov, Inc. to develop and administer the electrical licensing examination program. Candidates must first complete the appropriate application with the Arkansas Board of Electrical Examiners. Once approved for testing, the Board notifies the candidate that they are eligible to contact Prov to schedule the examination. The Arkansas Journeyman Electrician exam is listed by Prov as an examination available in English or Spanish. The official Arkansas electrical candidate information bulletin identifies the Arkansas Journeyman Electrician exam as a National Electrical Code-based exam. The current bulletin lists the Arkansas Journeyman Electrician examination as 60 questions with a 3-hour time allowance. The bulletin also states that all exams are graded against a cut score of 70%.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Arkansas Journeyman Electrician exam content outline includes grounding and bonding, general knowledge of the electrical trade and calculations, service, feeders, branch feeders and overcurrent protection, raceways and enclosures, conductors, motors and controls, utilization and general use equipment, special occupancies and equipment, low voltage circuits including alarms and communications, and safety. Because the exam covers several important trade areas, candidates should prepare with a balanced study plan. It is not enough to study only calculations or only code definitions. Candidates should review electrical theory, calculations, wiring methods, grounding, service equipment, branch circuits, motors, low voltage systems, safety, and general electrical trade knowledge. The strongest preparation routine combines reading, code lookup, calculation practice, flash card review, and timed practice questions. This product is based on the 2026 National Electrical Code and is designed for candidates preparing with the 2026 code cycle.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Arkansas electrical candidate information bulletin states that all examinations administered through the program are open book and timed. For the Arkansas Journeyman Electrician exam, the listed reference is NFPA 70, the National Electrical Code. Open-book testing gives candidates access to an approved reference, but it does not remove the need for preparation. Open-book electrical exams require speed and familiarity with the code book. A candidate who does not know how the National Electrical Code is organized may spend too much time searching for answers. A candidate who studies with the NEC regularly can move more efficiently between articles, sections, tables, definitions, and exceptions. Prov’s reference rules allow candidates to prepare reference materials using highlighting, underlining in pen only, and permanent tabs. The rules do not allow handwritten notes in reference books, moveable tabs, Post-it notes, photocopied documents added to reference books, photocopied versions of reference books, or test preparation study guides in the testing center.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: The Arkansas Board of Electrical Examiners is responsible for administering Arkansas laws governing the licensing of electricians. The Board also registers electrical apprentices and establishes standards for the performance of electrical work in the state. The Director of Code Enforcement has responsibility for enforcing these electrical laws. Arkansas law requires state licensing for individuals who are electricians, are engaged in electrical work, or use any title, sign, card, advertisement, or other device to indicate that they are engaged in electrical work. Because licensing is tied to the specific class of work, candidates should follow the requirements for the correct Arkansas electrical license class. The Board’s available electrical license classes include master electrician, journeyman electrician, residential master electrician, residential journeyman electrician, air conditioning electrician, and industrial maintenance electrician. The Arkansas Journeyman Electrician classification is the focus of this product.

pieces.t: Arkansas requires state licensing for individuals who perform electrical work or represent themselves as engaged in electrical work. The Board also establishes standards for the performance of electrical work in Arkansas, while code enforcement responsibilities are handled through the Department of Labor and Licensing structure. Arkansas recognizes multiple electrical license classifications, so candidates should select the correct license type before applying. The Master Electrician classification is separate from the journeyman, residential, air conditioning, industrial maintenance, and apprentice categories. Candidates should not schedule an exam until they are sure which examination is required for the license being sought. Continuing education is part of maintaining electrical licensure in Arkansas. The electrical licensing section identifies approved continuing education resources and tracking through StateReporting.com.

pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials
pieces.t: This Ultimate Combo includes multiple study formats so candidates can prepare from more than one angle. The Arkansas Master Electrician Study Guide supports topic-by-topic review. The Electrician Calculations Study Guide helps candidates slow down and strengthen math skills before test day. The National Electrical Code 2026 paperback with tabs supports code familiarity and reference speed. The Master Electrician Flash Cards are useful for short study sessions, quick review, terminology reinforcement, and memory building. The Online Test Success Kit adds practice-oriented exam review for candidates who want to work through questions and identify areas that need more attention. A strong study routine should include reading, practice, review, and repetition. Candidates should begin with the larger exam categories, including grounding and bonding, services and feeders, branch circuits and overcurrent protection, raceways, conductors, motors, utilization equipment, special occupancies, low voltage systems, safety, and calculations.

pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials
pieces.t: After reviewing each subject, candidates should practice exam questions and then return to the NEC to confirm the code basis for the answer. Calculations deserve special attention. Many candidates can perform electrical work confidently but still need dedicated review for exam calculations. Practice should include setting up the problem correctly, identifying the correct NEC table or rule, using the correct units, and avoiding common math mistakes. Repetition helps candidates become more comfortable with the steps instead of trying to relearn formulas during the exam. Code-book navigation should also be part of every study session. Candidates should practice using the table of contents, index, article structure, definitions, tables, notes, exceptions, and cross-references. The goal is not to memorize the entire NEC. The goal is to understand how the NEC is organized and how to find reliable answers quickly during a timed, open-book exam.
